title.narrative: Output 5.3. Increased capacity of Member States to design and deliver innovative, flexible and inclusive learning options, encompassing work-based learning and quality apprenticeships

description.narrative:
Partnership established between the Employers' Federation of Ceylon (EFC) and Tertiary and Vocational Education Commission (TVEC) on strengthening Skills passport system to support work-based learning through digital infrastructural enhancement of the "National Skills passport Secretariate". Vocational Training Authority of Sri Lanka (VTA) has upskilled 859 aspirant migrant workers targeting care sector employment abroad. ILO facilitated the partnership between the EFC and TVEC, in strengthening the Skills Passport system; through capacity and infrastructural enhancement of the “National Skills Passport Secretariat” by providing required HR and IT system development
The ILO developed human resource and IT system for the infrastructural enhancement of the “National Skills Passport Secretariat.
The ILO, with the support from the Government of Japan, collaborated with the Vocational authority of Sri Lanka in designing and implementing upskilling programme for migrant workers in the care sector
Organised a multi-stakeholder forum (in Jan 2022), in the theme of “Skilling Sri Lankan workforce towards Global talent pool”, to bring consensus among all key partners on vital importance of skills development of migrant workers. Technically assisted in establishment of the “Committee on Assessment and Development of Skills of Overseas Sri Lankans” (ADSOSL), including senior officials of Ministries of Education, Labour, Foreign Affairs, TVEC, and facilitated in convening the sessions. - Facilitated a resource sharing among TVET institutes for conducting skills assessment. (implemented by NAITA and DTET on sharing assessment centre facilities, and by VTA and SLITHM on referral for RPL registration and assessment).

Output 5.1. Increased capacity of Member States to identify current skills mismatches and anticipate future skill needs

description.narrative: Sri Lanka Institute of Tourism and Hotel Management (SLITHM) adopted and implemented a National Curricula Standard (NCS) for Hospitality and Employment sectors that benefited about 500 Migrant workers in the Tourism sector. The National Union of Seafarers (NUSS) established a tripartite partnership between Workers' organizations, Employers' organizations, and Government Sector to launch a maritime training programme, transforming 24 young aspirant migrant workers to become seafarers. TVEC conducted 620 RPL assessments for returned and aspirant migrant workers (186 for NVQ 3 and 434 for NVQ 8) - Completed 8 skills- gap filling programs for 78 returned migrant workers - Upskilled 859 aspirant migrant workers through Vocational Training Authority (VTA) of Sri Lanka. Sri Lanka Nidahas Sewaka Sangamaya (SLNSS/ workers organization) conducted 04 awareness programs for 185 Migrant Workers (68 M and 117 F) on skills development - Seamanship and maritime training provided for 24 returnee and aspiring migrant workers by the National Union of Seafarers, conducted by Mahapola Maritime Training Academy of Sri Lanka. Center for Working Women (CENWOR), a Workers' Organization launched a series of awareness campaigns in 10 Districts of Sri Lanka; reached about 1,168 migrant workers (M 275 and F 893), and referred 200 of them for skills assessment to TVEC. The ILO, through its Regular Budget Supplementary Allocation (RBSA), collaborated with SLITHM in training (Employment linked Training Program) conducted for Migrant Workers in the tourism sector. The ILO provided technical assistance to Sri Lanka Nidahas Sewaka Sangamaya (SLNSS) to create awareness among aspirant migrant workers on the importance of skilled migration, avenues for skills recognition through “Recognition of Prior Learning” (RPL) process, and safe migration opportunities, through “Migrant Recruitment Advisor” (MRA) portal introduced jointly with the ITUC.

title.narrative: 5.1.2. Number of Member States with institutionalized national or sectoral mechanisms to measure skills mismatches and anticipate future skill needs
Output 5.1. Increased capacity of Member States to identify current skills mismatches and anticipate future skill needs

description.narrative:
Tertiary and Vocational Education Commission (TVEC), and sectoral Skills Council created better awareness among the government officials and the general public on skills demanded by the industry.
In coordination with TVEC and Ministry of Labour and Foreign Employment (MoLFE), the Workers Organization (Employers' Federation of Ceylon/ EFC) organized a stakeholder consultation to ascertain in the aspiration of the employers on skills passport initiative. The ILO provided technical and collaborated with Employers Federation of Ceylon (EFC) to organize a stakeholder consultation to ascertain the aspirations of the employers in relation to the Skills Passport, in liaison with key stakeholders.
The ILO facilitated collaborated with TVEC and Sector Skills Councils to conduct a Webinar series on skills development for Industry-demanded occupations, in par with World Youth Skills Day 2021.

description.narrative: The President announced on 19th July 2023 the establishment of an inter-ministerial action committee under the leadership of the Minister of Labour and Foreign Employment, and President’s Secretary, comprising key secretaries from various ministries, including Education, Finance, Tourism, Fisheries, Transport, Plantation and Industry which help grow resilient businesses and decent jobs through strategic interventions in the areas of: a) Job creation, b) skills enhancement, and (c) institutional reform. The ILO has supported its tripartite constituents to develop a "Labour Market Recovery and Transformation Strategy (LMRTS)," as requested by the Government of Sri Lanka. The LMRTS is based on dialogue among stakeholders and relevant research, particularly the results of a recent rapid assessment of the impact of the multiple crises on micro, small, and medium enterprises (MSMEs). The tripartite sub-committee was formed in March 2023, and tripartite discussions with members from other ministries, the Employers Federation of Ceylon (EFC), and trade unions were led by the Ministry of Labour and Foreign Employment
